instructions: Put the wakame in a small bowl, cover it with cold water, and leave it for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, whisk together 6 tbsp ponzu, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sesame oil, 1/4 tsp salt and 1 tbsp sesame seeds.
Drain the tofu. Cut it into 1/2 inch cubes, handling it gently so it keeps its shape.
Wash and dry the lettuce. Tear it into bite-size pieces and arrange it on a large platter.
Scatter the corn over the lettuce. Halve the cherry tomatoes and add them.
Squeeze the wakame dry and add it to the platter with the tofu.
Just before serving, drizzle about two thirds of the dressing over the salad. Serve with the rest of the dressing in a small cup on the table.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook leads (4.69 from 22): torn lettuce with cubed silken tofu, wakame, corn and tomato, in a ponzu, soy sauce and sesame oil dressing with sesame seeds. Amounts are doubled from its 2 servings. Shiso and the yuzu kosho are left out. Cooking with Yoshiko makes a blended onion and carrot sesame dressing instead, and uses tamari to make it gluten-free. Ponzu usually has wheat soy sauce, and some brands have bonito, so the list asks for one without it to stay vegan.
